clue.text: Superficial need to sort inside refuse container

indicators.note: inside tells us the reworked letters sit within the word that follows

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for rubbish, here split open to take the middle letters

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so the preceding word's letters get put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A shallow person feels the urge to tidy up the inside of a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for a large builder's rubbish container; the rearranged letters of 'need' go inside it to give SKIN-DEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the outer layer, which is exactly what superficial means.

clue.text: The sea on the shore slave listened to

indicators.note: something listened to is heard rather than read, so we want a word that sounds like the slave

parts.note: a serf was a medieval bonded labourer, close to a slave

explanation.surface: A slave by the coast listens to the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the foaming water of waves as they break against the beach.

clue.text: Four regularly visiting pub for a laugh

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so these letters go inside the word for a drinking house

parts.note: an inn is a pub, opened up to take the selected letters

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so we keep every other letter of the word before it

parts.note: first and third letters of the number word

explanation.surface: A group of four drop in on the local pub just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something was done 'in fun' means it was meant as a joke, not seriously, so for a laugh.

clue.text: Retail outlet where staff have nothing to do?

definitions.text: Retail outlet where staff have nothing to do?

parts.words: Retail outlet where staff have nothing to do?
parts.note: surface reading: a lazy shop whose workers are idle

parts.words: where staff have nothing to do?
parts.note: setter's reading: staff free of any duty, i.e. the airport shop selling goods free of tax

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' means both an obligation and an import tax; an airport shop selling goods exempt from tax is read as one whose staff are exempt from work.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a shop, usually at an airport, selling goods on which no customs tax is charged.

clue.text: Bring me up part of tree to make board

parts.note: surface padding that pairs with 'up' to make the instruction read naturally

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards
bark is the outer covering of a tree trunk

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have a piece of a tree brought up so a plank can be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a noun for a wooden plank, but it is the verb meaning to get on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or aircraft, the same as boarding it.

clue.text: Keen to put name forward for bender

indicators.note: the instruction moves the letter standing for name earlier in the word, a small rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written; its N (name) is shifted forward two places

explanation.surface: Someone eager to nominate a person for a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; move it from fourth place to second in KEEN. 'Bender' looks like a drinking binge but is something that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint that lets the leg flex, so it is literally a thing that bends.

clue.text: Square leg, that bowler may aim at?

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: A cricket fielding position at square leg, a natural target for the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, but the words split: a square number and a slang word for a leg. The bowler is at a skittle alley, not a cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is one of the skittles a player bowls a ball to knock down.

clue.text: Pharaoh for one training tiny page

indicators.note: training knocks something into a new shape, so the following letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pharaoh coaches a little page boy at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a ruler of ancient Egypt, so he is an example of a native of that country.

clue.text: Very precise mail that came to be translated

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters arriving from abroad need a very exact translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematical is used loosely for anything done with rigorous, numerical exactness.

clue.text: Judge information technology leads to renovation

parts.note: a ref (referee) judges a match
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A judge's computer expertise prompts a makeover of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a restoration or overhaul, typically of a ship or shop, so a renovation.

clue.text: Times covering Antrim town in flattering speech

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the first word surrounds the town

parts.note: as in three by four, meaning multiplied by
Larne is a port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A newspaper's report on a town in Northern Ireland is full of flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means the multiplication sign, read as 'by'. Blarney Stone, the source of the word, is in County Cork.
explanation.definitionFit: Blarney is smooth, flattering talk meant to charm or persuade.

clue.text: Extra tea that's earned by sinking a red?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the extra spoonful added to the teapot beyond one per person

definitions.text: that's earned by sinking a red?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in snooker, potting a red ball scores a single point

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker each red ball potted scores one point, so a red sunk earns 'one' for the pot. The tea custom is a British habit when brewing in a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the traditional extra spoonful of tea leaves added for the pot itself.

clue.text: Support His Excellency? Extremely silly to predict

parts.note: a prop holds something up
the abbreviation used for an ambassador's title

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters only

parts.note: the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Backing an ambassador might seem a foolish way to forecast the future.
explanation.definitionFit: To prophesy is to foretell future events, as a prophet does.

clue.text: Rugby dropped, not having enough time

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
to shed is to drop or cast off

explanation.surface: A rugby player was left out of the side because there was no time.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling rushed means being hurried and pressed, lacking the time one needs.

clue.text: Spy ring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an agent placed long in advance and left inactive until needed
second meaning: a small hoop earring worn to keep a pierced hole open

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'spy ring' suggests an espionage network; the two words define separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is both a dormant secret agent and a plain hoop earring kept in a piercing.

clue.text: A chap with daughter, a girl

parts.note: taken as written
a chap is a man
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man and his daughter, with the daughter being a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a female first name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: A fat book put into words

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book
to utter is to say aloud, express in speech

explanation.surface: A thick volume finally written up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fat book' reads as a thick volume, but 'A fat' is the definition and the book is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is a dairy fat churned from cream.

clue.text: A piece of paper worth keeping

definitions.text: A piece of paper worth keeping

parts.words: A piece of paper worth keeping
parts.note: surface reading: any valuable document, like a certificate
setter's reading: paper means a newspaper, and the piece is an article clipped out of it and saved

explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a sheet of stationery but means a newspaper; a piece of it kept is an item snipped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an article clipped from a newspaper or magazine and kept for reference.

clue.text: Generous founder of prize putting English last

indicators.note: the instruction moves the letter for English to the end of the word, a small rearrangement

parts.note: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel Prizes; his E (English) is moved to the end

explanation.surface: A generous benefactor endows a prize, with English coming last.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the usual abbreviation for English; shift it from fourth place to the end of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean high-minded and magnanimous, showing generosity of spirit.

clue.text: I'd to abandon Crusoe's man in brawl

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so those letters come out of the name

parts.note: Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's companion in Defoe's novel
the contraction, its letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone longs to desert Robinson Crusoe's servant in the middle of a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or scuffle, as in 'joining the fray'.

clue.text: Old conspiracy includes one daring feat

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside, so the plot wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a plot is a secret scheme
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old conspiracy had at its heart one daring act.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or adventurous deed, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: This Highlander may give a toss

definitions.text: This Highlander may give a toss

parts.words: This Highlander may give a toss
parts.note: surface reading: a Scot who, for once, actually cares, as in 'not give a toss'
setter's reading: a long wooden pole thrown end over end at Highland games

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a toss' is British slang for caring; here the toss is literal, at the Scottish Highland games, and the Highlander is a Highland object, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber is the heavy tree-trunk pole flung in a traditional Scottish athletic event.

clue.text: This garden ridiculously short?

parts.note: surface reading: a garden that is absurdly small
setter's reading: a garden word that is also a unit of three feet, absurdly short for any plot

explanation.walkthrough: The word is the American term for a garden and also a length of just three feet, so a garden measured by its own name would be tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the ground around a house is called by this word, which is also a three-foot measure.

clue.text: Jokiness of orderly convulsed with laughter at first

indicators.note: convulsed means thrown into spasms, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly doubled up with laughter at a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like an adjective or a hospital attendant, but it is just letters to be mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is dry, quaint humour, so it amounts to jokiness.
